title: Protocol for lentiviral knock down in mouse ES cells
protocol: Plate Cos-7 cells in Cos-7 medium at ~40% confluency on 10 cm dishes, ensuring even distribution of cells over the plate.
Mix 300 ul DMEM low glucose with 24 μl Fugene 6 by flicking; incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Mix plasmids: 2 μg pRSV-rev, 2 μg pMDLg/pRRE, 2 μg pMD2.G, and 2 μg pLKO-short hairpin construct.
Add contents of Tube 1 to Tube 2; mix by flicking and incubate for 20-30 min at room temperature.
Add mixture to Cos-7 cells.
Replace the medium of transfected Cos-7 cells with 10 ml ES medium/10 cm dish.
Plate IB10 ES cells on gelatinized dishes at 4.4 x 10e4 cells/10 cm dish.
Collect viral supernatant from Cos-7 cells using a syringe and filter through 0.45 μm low protein binding filter to remove cells.
Add fresh ES medium to the Cos-7 cells.
Remove the medium from the IB10 cells.
Supplement the viral supernatant with 8 μg/ml polybrene.
Mix the supplemented viral supernatant and add it to the IB10 cells.
Use 10 ml of undiluted viral supernatant to infect one 10 cm dish of IB10 cells.
Repeat the infection process on day 4 as described for day 3.
Add fresh ES medium to the Cos-7 cells.
Optionally, repeat the infection once more on day 5 as described for day 3.
Discard the Cos-7 cells after optional repetition.
Refresh the medium of infected IB10 cells daily with ES medium containing 1.8 μg/ml puromycin starting 1-2 days after the last infection.
Assess the condition of the IB10 cells to ensure clear growth and formation of small colonies before initiating puromycin selection.
Wait an additional day if necessary for proper cell growth before starting puromycin selection.
Analyze the cells on day 11 for alkaline phosphatase colony staining or RT-qPCR to determine knock down efficiency.
Mix 70 μl of beta-mercaptoethanol stock with 100 ml H2O.
Aliquot and store the beta-mercaptoethanol solution at -20°C.
Add 6 ml non-essential amino acids (Lonza 13-114E).
Mix 60 μl LIF (500 U/ml final) into the mixture (Gibco 13275-029).
